The *Ulūkaṅgapañha* ("The Owl") is a discourse in the seventh book of the *Milindapañha*, belonging to the late canonical or post-canonical collection of Pali texts [SuttaCentral]. Like other sections of this division, the text draws upon the qualities and habits of a specific entity—here, an owl—as a simile for the virtues and spiritual practices to be cultivated by a practitioner [SuttaCentral]. The discourse is recorded in relation to the *Paṭisallānasutta* of the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* (SN 56.2), and SuttaCentral catalogues three translations of the work across three languages [SuttaCentral].

Much of this reuse stems from the formulaic structure shared among the simile sections of the *Milindapañha*, including close structural parallels with the *Cakkavattiṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.10), *Ākāsaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.6), *Sakkaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.9), *Padumaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.3.2), and *Sīhaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.6.1) [DharmaNexus].
